title: Write the question bank
description: A tenant administrator (the exam author) keeps the question bank: categories (a tree), tags, questions with their answer options, and the links between them. In the question bank screen they list questions, open the editor, save a new or changed question, and delete one. A question may be a new version of an older one (lineage). The system refuses a category that is its own ancestor, a parent that does not exist, a second child on one question version, a version number that does not rise, and the deletion of a category or question that still has children. RUNNER SCOPE: the scenario plays create, whole replace and delete of a category, a question and an answer option; the tree and lineage refusals (parent_cycle, parent_not_found, version_not_increasing, lineage_branch, the has_children refusals) are enforced by the code and its tests but are not in the dry run, because the active category definition on the dry-run tenant does not yet declare parent_id.
preconditions: module exam installed in the tenant
the entity definitions of the exam pack are active

tasks.result: the author sees the list of questions, or the list of another authoring type (categories, tags, answer options); the write actions show only to a holder of the authoring permission

a question, answer option, category or tag record is created or replaced as a whole; the answer carries the record without the fields the caller may not see; a tree or lineage rule that fails is 422 with the reason (parent_cycle, parent_not_found, lineage_branch, version_not_increasing, lineage_active_conflict)
the record is removed (soft delete); a category or question that still has a live child is 409 (category_has_children, question_has_children)

inputs: entity type (question, answer_option, category, tag, question_tag)
optional expected last event number on change
refusals: a role without ExamAuthoringWrite (CANDIDATE, PROCESS_OPERATOR, TASK_WORKER) is refused with 403, nothing written
an entity type that is not one of the ten authoring types is the same 404 on all three routes
a tenant administrator of another tenant gets a 404 for this tenant's record id
a body naming a field the caller's field restrictions hide is refused
a stale expected_last_event_global_seq is 409

title: Build an exam
description: A tenant administrator assembles an exam: title, pass mark, number of attempts, time limit, availability window, the policy for a candidate leaving the exam tab, the sections, the question rules (how many questions of which category or tag) and the manually pinned questions. They also assign the exam to candidates. The builder screens are shown only to a holder of the authoring permission. Every save is an authoring write of BP-EXAM-01 on the exam types. STAYS PARTIAL: the assignment of an exam to a candidate has no route and no screen (only Authoring.create_assignment, called by the mix seed task, REQ-582), so the last task of this process cannot be done by a person; the builder write path itself is played by the scenario.
preconditions: BP-EXAM-01 has produced the questions the exam draws on

tasks.result: the list of exams and one exam with its sections, question rules and pinned questions; a user without the authoring permission gets the shell's forbidden page

exam, exam_section, exam_question_rule, exam_question_rule_tag and exam_manual_question records are written; an exam edited while sessions are live does not change a session already started (the session keeps its own snapshot)
an exam_assignment record says which candidate may sit which exam; today only the mix seed task writes it, no route and no screen (see orphans-exam.md)

outputs: the exam in status draft or active
refusals: same as BP-EXAM-01: 403 without the permission, uniform 404 for an unknown type or another tenant's record

title: Find and start an exam
description: A candidate opens the exam list, sees the exams assigned to them and open now, and starts one. The system checks in this order: the exam exists and is active, the candidate is assigned, the exam is not archived, the availability window is open, the attempts are not used up, no session of theirs is open. It then draws the questions (with a fresh seed) and fixes them in the session. If a session is already open the answer names it so the screen can continue it. STAYS PARTIAL (no runner scenario): a candidate can start only an exam that is assigned to them, and nothing but the mix seed task writes an assignment (no route, no screen: Authoring.create_assignment, lib/letflow/modules/exam/authoring.ex:131). A runner process has no seed step, so the start cannot be played at API level without inventing behaviour. Needs: an assignment route or an exam_assignment fixture of the runner. The refusals of the candidate's session routes are played by BP-EXAM-07.
preconditions: an active exam assigned to the candidate, inside its availability window, with attempts left (BP-EXAM-02)

tasks.result: a page of the exams the candidate may start now (page size and cursor are validated: 400 on a bad value)
201 with the session and its questions, without the answer key; the candidate is the caller's own id, never a value from the body

refusals: not assigned: 403; archived: 403
exam not active, outside the availability window, attempts exhausted: 422
a session of the same candidate is already open: 409 with the id of that session
a pinned question that is missing or not active: 422 with a constant text; the exam content or snapshot failing: 503 with a constant text
an exam_id that is not a UUID is answered like an exam that is not active (422)

title: Sit the exam and submit
description: The candidate answers the questions. Each answer is saved at once (single, multiple, true/false, likert, short text) with the time spent; the screen reports tab switches, loss of focus and leaving full screen. The server alone judges the deadline and what a signal does (warn or submit) from the exam's own policy. The candidate submits; the system scores the objective questions, and a session with a short-text answer waits for the examiner (BP-EXAM-05). A session past its deadline is closed by the system. STAYS PARTIAL (no runner scenario): it needs an open session, which BP-EXAM-03 cannot produce at API level (no assignment route). The refusals of the session routes (404 on an id that is not the caller's) are played by BP-EXAM-07. Needs the same assignment route or fixture.

tasks.result: the session state with the questions and the answers saved so far; never is_correct, likert weights or the explanation
the answer is stored; the answer carries the seconds remaining

one signal event is recorded unless it falls inside the debounce window; the answer says the action taken (from the exam's on_tab_switch policy), the event count, whether to warn, and the submission when the policy submits
the session is scored and closed with score and pass/fail, or marked grading pending when a short-text answer needs the examiner; a second submit returns the same outcome

inputs: answers (selected option ids or text) with time spent
refusals: a session id that is not the caller's own, does not exist, or is not a UUID: the same 404 body
answer after the deadline or on a closed session: refused; a question that is not in the session: 400; an option that is not the question's: 400; a wrong answer shape: 400
a signal type other than the three: 400; a signal on a closed session or after the deadline: refused
a body with a candidate id, a score or an action_taken is not read (there is no such parameter)

title: Grade short-text answers
description: An examiner (today a tenant administrator) opens the grading queue, sees the short-text answers waiting for a mark (optionally for one exam, in a chosen language), opens one answer, and gives a score between zero and the maximum of the question. When the last waiting answer of a session is marked the system finalises the session (score, pass/fail). An answer is marked once. STAYS PARTIAL (no runner scenario): it needs a submitted session with a short-text answer waiting for the examiner, which needs BP-EXAM-03 and BP-EXAM-04 first (no assignment route). The refusals of the grading routes (403 for a candidate, 422 for a body with a grader id, 404 on an unknown answer) are played by BP-EXAM-07.
preconditions: a session submitted with a short-text answer and status grading pending (BP-EXAM-04)

tasks.result: a page of waiting answers of this tenant only, filter by exam_id
the question stem and the candidate's answer
the mark is stored with the caller as grader; when it is the last waiting answer the session becomes final and the answer says its status

refusals: a role other than the administrator (CANDIDATE, PROCESS_OPERATOR, PROCESS_DESIGNER, TASK_WORKER, AGENT_RUNNER, TENANT_AUDITOR): 403 with one identical body; no token: 401
any key but score in the body, a score below zero or not a number: 422; above the question's maximum: 422
a session or question that is missing, malformed, of another tenant, already graded (on the read) or not short text: the same 404
an answer already graded, on the grade route: 409

title: See my results and get the certificate
description: The candidate opens the list of their finished sessions with score, pass/fail and certificate status, opens one result, and, when the session is passed and the exam issues certificates, asks for the certificate and downloads it as a PDF. The first request issues it; every later request returns the same one. STAYS PARTIAL (no runner scenario): it needs a finished session of a candidate, which the missing assignment route makes unreachable at API level; the certificate refusal on a session that is not the caller's (404) is played by BP-EXAM-07.
preconditions: a finished (and, for the certificate, passed) session of the candidate (BP-EXAM-04, BP-EXAM-05)

tasks.result: only the caller's own sessions, with the exam title, score, passed flag and certificate id
200 on first issue, with a one-time public_handle; 200 with the same certificate, without public_handle, afterwards
the certificate as application/pdf with a public verification address

inputs: optional exam_id filter and page cursor on the list
refusals: a session that is not the caller's, missing or not a UUID: the same 404
grading still pending, session not submitted, exam without certificates, session not passed: 409 with a distinct text each

title: Security: roles and crafted input are refused
description: The permission matrix of the exam module and the crafted-input refusals, at API level: the candidate cannot write the question bank, read the grading queue or mark an answer (403); the candidate's calls on a session id that is not theirs get the same 404 as a missing one; an administrator naming an unknown authoring type gets 404; a grading body with a grader identity is refused 422 before any lookup. Permission matrix: ExamSessionStart, ExamSessionRead, ExamSessionSave, ExamSessionSubmit, ExamSessionReportEvent, ExamCertificateIssue are granted to CANDIDATE by the module manifest; ExamAuthoringWrite, ExamGradingRead and ExamGradingWrite have no role grant and are held only through the core rules (PLATFORM_ADMIN, TENANT_ADMIN). The runner script covers a part (status automated for those steps); the rest is listed below as planned.
preconditions: tenant bilimbaga with the exam module installed
a candidate login and a tenant administrator login

tasks.result: 403 on every one; the matrix (candidate: six session permissions only) is proven by test/letflow/modules/exam/exam_authoring_test.exs (T-4), grading_queue_test.exs and grading_mark_test.exs (G-perm-1, all denied roles one 403 body, no token 401). [automated: scenario steps s2-s5]

another candidate's session (same tenant), another tenant's session and a missing id all give one identical 404: the owner check folds session_not_found and not_owner into Response.not_found; the prefix scoping hides other tenants. [automated for a missing id: steps s6-s9; own-vs-other candidate and cross-tenant (a token of tenant A against tenant B's ids): planned, needs a second candidate login and a two-tenant runner; proven today by exam_sessions_test.exs and exam_snapshot_router_test.exs]
an authoring type that does not exist is 404 (T-6 in exam_authoring_test.exs); a grade body with any key but score is 422 before the lookup (reject_unknown_grade_keys). [automated: steps s10-s12]

crafted input: a signal type outside the three is 400, an answer or signal after the stored deadline is refused (the server compares its own clock to the session's stored expiry), a question or option not in the session is 400; planned as a runner scenario: needs an open session and a short exam, which only a seeded exam can give

refusals: no token or an invalid token: 401 (planned as a runner step: the runner has no no-credential actor yet)
unknown host: not answered by the tenant (planned: host lookup belongs to the tenant-admin / platform area)

upload types and limits, voice input, webhook input and the old shared-access address: the exam router has no such route (grep of lib/letflow/modules/exam/router.ex for upload, multipart, webhook, shared: no match); nothing to test here
separation of duties: the examiner role is held by the tenant administrator only, and the grader id is the caller's, never from the body (automated, step s11)
